note: Written 5 Sep 2026 for Tranche 2. TWO DISAGREEMENTS ARE ON THIS RECORD AND NEITHER IS RESOLVED. The architect: the HABS sheet says 'Architect: Robert Mills'; the Library's own catalogue line for the same item, the Valentine which owns the house, and Venture Richmond all say Alexander Parris. Both are recorded, neither is changed, and nothing in this corpus should be built on either until a third surface is read. The style word: the surveyor calls it 'Late Georgian' and describes exactly what this node calls Federal -- 'clear wall spaces instead of panelling; delicately carved ornament instead of excessive applied ornament'. That is the second record in this cluster where a surveyor declines the Georgian/Federal boundary the corpus draws. Worth carrying for the node's own prose, which says the Southern Federal house 'spreads' and is one room deep: this one is a THREE-STOREY town house over a basement with an oval salon on the axis at the rear, which is the urban half of the variant the node's description does not describe.
